# Original embedded font notebook

`fonts.ts` adds one two-page original fixture to cover the embedded-font gaps in the exploratory corpus: the research/math documents (`attention`, `resnet`, `bitcoin`), multilingual samples (`udhr-chinese`, `japanese-leaflet`, `un-arabic`), and embedded-font characteristics of the archival/print samples (`pdfa2`, `pdfx4`). It is an original miniature notebook, not a reproduction of any sample's text, artwork, layout, or font data.

## Ownership and reproducibility

`font-programs.ts` authors both font binaries deterministically from individually drawn, geometric outlines. All source code, glyph skeletons, prose, mathematical layout, and garden-seal artwork were created for this repository and use its MPL-2.0 license. There are no downloaded fonts, system-font dependencies, external assets, or asset-license exceptions. Unicode characters, arithmetic identities, and standard font/PDF wire formats are used as information rather than copied artwork. The programs are generated by TypeScript at test time; no platform-native font tools or shaping libraries are involved.

The binary authors follow the [Microsoft OpenType specification](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/otff), [TrueType outline format](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/glyf), [Adobe CFF format](https://adobe-type-tools.github.io/font-tech-notes/pdfs/5176.CFF.pdf), and [Adobe Type 2 charstring format](https://adobe-type-tools.github.io/font-tech-notes/pdfs/5177.Type2.pdf). Those specifications are references, not redistributed assets. No example font or outline bytes were copied from them.

## Executed characteristics

- Page 1 embeds a complete original TrueType program using `FontFile2`, a Type 0 font, a `CIDFontType2` descendant, `Identity-H`, and `CIDToGIDMap /Identity`. The program has the required `head`, `hhea`, `maxp`, `hmtx`, `cmap`, `name`, `OS/2`, and `post` tables plus simple unhinted `glyf` outlines and long `loca` offsets. Tests check every table checksum and the whole-font checksum, alignment, glyph count, and final glyph offset.
- Page 2 embeds an original CID-keyed CFF 1 program in `FontFile3 /Subtype /CIDFontType0C` through a Type 0 font with a `CIDFontType0` descendant. The program includes a name, Top DICT, custom strings, ROS, CID charset, FDSelect, FDArray/private dictionary, and Type 2 charstrings. Each glyph contains actual outline commands and advance width, rather than a placeholder stream.
- Both pages use the embedded programs for every visible character. The multilingual repertoire includes Chinese character groups `山川日月` and `木火土金水`, Japanese `山の川と月`, and Arabic `باب` and `سلام`. The Arabic content supplies original contextual glyph shapes and a lam-alef ligature in visual order. `ToUnicode` maps the ligature to U+FEFC; PDFium normalizes it and extracts the ordinary logical Arabic word `سلام`. This is preservation of pre-shaped text, not a claim that Mondrian implements Unicode bidi or Arabic shaping.
- Mathematics uses positioned superscripts, fraction rules/numerators/denominators, a summation with bounds, an integral with bounds, a radical, Greek letters, and a second rendering of the original CJK glyphs. The typography is intentionally an angular display face rather than an imitation of a downloaded research paper.

## Independent proof and limits

The private visual test opens both the original PDF and the parser/serializer roundtrip in pinned PDFium, requires valid cross-reference tables, and compares **every page's** size, rotation, extracted text, and exact raw pixels. It separately checks the intended English, Chinese, Japanese, Arabic, and mathematical text. Both pages have visually reviewed 96 dpi PNG baselines. Geometry has generous margins; the larger baseline makes the original small text and mathematical bounds reviewable.

Two negative controls independently regenerate only one embedded program at a time with empty glyph outlines while retaining font names, widths, Unicode mappings, layout, and page content. The same PDFium proof must report changed pixels on that program's page, unchanged pixels on the other page, and unchanged extracted characters. This demonstrates that the renderer uses each embedded font program rather than silently substituting a fallback. Extracted whitespace may change with the empty glyph bounds and is ignored only in these negative controls; the real input/output comparison requires identical text.

All assertions are private regression checks and add no semver commitments. No parser production changes were needed. This closes the lack of real embedded TrueType/CFF/CID programs, pre-shaped Arabic, CJK/Japanese extraction, and positioned mathematical typesetting. It does not claim a general-purpose CJK font, OpenType GSUB/GPOS shaping, hinted/composite/variable font coverage, a complete mathematical layout engine, PDF/A or PDF/X certification, or parity with every production font found on the internet. These are font/viewer capabilities beyond this fixture's stated parser-preservation contract.

From `packages/mondrian`, run:

```sh
MONDRIAN_PDF_ARTIFACT_MODE=verify pnpm exec vp test run tests/private/original-fonts.test.ts tests/private/visual-regressions/original-fonts.test.ts
```
